Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) totally fun first (i.e., Entertainment game reappropriated), 
        (2) mostly fun first (i.e., design workshop with disabled stakeholders),
        (3) both fun and utility first (i.e., design workshop with diverse stakeholders), 
        (4) mostly utility first (i.e., primary utilitarian mechanic designed first),
        (5) totally utility first (i.e., made by clinicians or specialists, fun incorporated later)
reasoning: The work is an empirical/mixed-methods study to understand BLV people’s digital content creation needs and to inform accessibility and technology design. There is no game or entertainment system; the focus is on utility: accessibility, creative support tools, and social change. Design ideas are discussed as implications for accessibility research rather than as a fun-first or co-designed playful system, aligning with a mostly utility-first orientation.

        (3) both symmetrical and asymmetrical (i.e., pandemic with its similar turn structure but different character abilities),

reasoning: The work is not a game or interactive system with roles; it is a mixed-methods survey and interview study of BLV creators’ experiences.
